Forming a comprehensive full-stack "Sense + Compute" capability

SynSense, powered by its core neuromorphic intelligence technology, offers products widely applicable in scenarios such as intelligent interaction (AR/VR), intelligent monitoring, smart livestock farming, intelligent security, industrial monitoring, smart vehicles and etc.

Recognized by industry authorities, the company serves as a key chain leader in advancing ecosystem commercialization. We have established collaborations including Huawei, CETHIK, and Ningxia State Farm, and signed a proof-of-concept (POC) agreement with PICO, jointly accelerating the industrialization of neuromorphic technologies.
Physical/Chemical Property Testing
Prepare test plans, test reports, and related technical documents to ensure the integrity and traceability of test data.
Process Optimization Support
Collaborate with electrode R&D and production line teams on sample validation, and provide constructive feedback based on practical testing.
Participate in establishing quality standards and control processes for electrode products.

Master’s degree or above in Microelectronics, Semiconductor, Physics, Materials, Electronic Engineering, or a related field. 3-5 years of experience in electrode testing or related hardware testing. Familiarity with testing and using neural probes (e.g., microelectrode arrays) or BCI chips is preferred.
Professional Qualifications
· Equipment Operation: Proficient in operating test equipment such as electrochemical workstations and impedance analyzers. Knowledge of characterization tools like SEM and profilometers is required.

· Professional Knowledge: Familiar with key electrode performance metrics (impedance, charge injection capacity, signal-to-noise ratio, etc.) and their testing methodologies. Familiar with applying CNN, LSTM, Transformer in sequence data modeling.
Preferred Qualifications
Neural Signal Processing and Decoding

Develop decoding algorithms and conduct data processing/analysis for neural signals (e.g., EEG, ECoG, single-unit Spikes, peripheral nerve signals) in BCI systems. Design and implement algorithms for signal preprocessing (denoising, filtering, artifact removal), feature extraction, and neural decoding.
Establish a neural signal annotation system, analyze the correlation between data and physiological function, and build an automated processing pipeline from raw data to feature space.

Collaborate with hardware/embedded teams on system integration and debugging to ensure algorithm effectiveness in practical implantable systems. Able to operate signal acquisition equipment and assist in designing acquisition protocols and experiments.

Master’s degree or above in Neural Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, Signal Processing, or a related field. 5+ years of experience in signal processing / machine learning algorithm development.

· Signal Processing Skills: Familiar with characteristics and processing methods of neural signals (EEG, ECoG, EMG, spike potentials, etc.). Proficient in signal processing techniques like wavelet transform, time-frequency analysis, and independent component analysis.

· Machine/Deep Learning Skills: Proficient in Python (or MATLAB) for data processing. Experienced in machine learning algorithms (SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost) or deep learning frameworks (PyTorch/TensorFlow). Familiar with applying CNN, LSTM, Transformer in sequence data modeling.
· Mathematical Foundation: Solid mathematical background, familiar with probability theory, statistics, linear algebra, and optimization theory.

Experience with invasive BCIs (Spike/LFP decoding) is preferred. Experience in closed-loop neuromodulation algorithm development is a plus. Publications in top-tier conferences or patents are advantageous.

Analog & Mixed-Signal Circuit Design: Design low-noise, low-power analog front-end (AFE) circuits for neural signal recording, including key modules such as instrumentation amplifiers, filters, and analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). Possess design experience with large-scale ADCs, on-chip signal processing, and high-density sensor interfaces.

Digital Logic & System Integration: Responsible for chip digital logic design (RTL design, synthesis, STA, etc.), support FPGA prototype verification, and lead chip layout design, verification, tape-out, and interaction with foundries.

· Analog/Mixed-Signal Skills: Solid professional background in analog and mixed-signal IC design, familiar with the design of modules such as low-noise instrumentation amplifiers, SAR/ΔΣ ADCs, DACs, and PLLs.
· Digital Design Skills: Proficient in Verilog/SystemVerilog, familiar with ASIC front-end design flow (RTL design, synthesis, formal verification, STA), and knowledgeable about DFT design.
· Tools & Platforms: Proficient in using EDA tools such as Cadence Virtuoso, Synopsys, or Mentor for full-custom circuit design and simulation.
· Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Ability to collaborate closely with neuroscience and materials science teams, and capable of professional technical communication in English.
Intelligent Monitoring: High-Precision Displacement Monitoring System

SynSense leverages the high-dynamic vision monitoring capabilities of its neuromorphic chips to launch two solutions: an automated calf behavior monitoring system and a precision spraying control system for cows.

The automated calf behavior monitoring system enables real-time event-based analysis of calf activity levels, providing early warning of abnormal behaviors and effectively replacing traditional inspection methods that rely on manual experience.

The precision cow spraying control system utilizes the unique characteristics of neuromorphic technology to achieve “on-demand spraying.” This ensures cow welfare and alleviates heat stress while achieving efficient water utilization.
Its technology is built around the principles of sensing-computing integration and ultra-low power consumption, enabling highly efficient and responsive intelligent systems .

SynSense has earned prestigious accolades including the CES Innovation Award and the Ministry of Science and Technology’s Disruptive Innovation Award. Looking ahead, the company plans to expand into the upstream brain-computer ecosystem by integrating “electrode + chip” modules, contributing China’s vision and solutions to the global AI industry.

The Speck is an ultra-low power event-driven neuromorphic processor combined with an event-driven vision sensor on a single chip. It was developed by SynSense AG, a neuromorphic engineering startup based in Zurich, Switzerland.

It comprises 9 layers of convolution combined with pooling, that can be freely connected to each other. The layers can additionally be operated as dense fully connected layers for last layer classification.
It has additional input preprocessing and decision readout blocks to make it out-of-the-box integratable in diverse environments and use cases.
